:::{#exm-density-limit-jump}
#### The density limit at a jump

At a point where $f$ is not continuous,
the limit can differ from the chosen value $f(x)$.
For $X \sim \text{Uniform}(0, 1)$ with the density $f$ of @def-uniform,
which sets $f(1) = 1$ and $f(x) = 0$ for $x > 1$,
and for $\change > 0$:

$$
\ba
\Pr(1 \le X < 1 + \change)
&= \Pr(1 \le X \le 1 + \change)
&& \text{(} \Pr(X = 1 + \change) = 0 \text{)} \\
&= \int_1^{1 + \change} f(x)\,dx
&& \text{(definition of the density)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(} f = 0 \text{ on } (1, 1 + \change] \text{; one point does not change an integral)}
\ea
$$

So the limit of $\Pr(1 \le X < 1 + \change) / \change$ at $x = 1$ is 0,
although $f(1) = 1$.
By @prp-density-limit-right-derivative,
0 is also the right derivative of $\cdf$ at 1,
matching the slope of 0 on the right in @exm-density-vs-CDF.

:::
